questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a painless papule on his right hand that has evolved over 2 weeks into an ulcer with a black eschar surrounded by non-pitting oedema. He handles animal hides regularly. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.exp: Cutaneous anthrax caused by Bacillus anthracis presents with a painless ulcer with a characteristic black eschar (malignant pustule) and significant non-pitting oedema. Exposure to animal products (hides, wool, bone meal) is classic.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman has widespread scaly plaques on her scalp and body with nail pitting and onycholysis. She is planning pregnancy. Which systemic therapy is ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED?
questions.exp: Acitretin is a teratogen with a very long half-life and women must avoid pregnancy for 3 years after stopping. Methotrexate also requires contraception but only for 3 months. Acitretin carries the strictest pregnancy contraindication among systemic psoriasis drugs.

questions.q: A 22-year-old male presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on his trunk. Slit skin smear shows AFB. Lepromin test is negative. Histology shows foamy macrophages with bacilli in globi. What is the classification?
questions.exp: Lepromatous leprosy (LL) has negative lepromin test (poor cell-mediated immunity), high bacterial load with AFB-laden foamy macrophages (Virchow cells) forming globi, and widespread lesions. It is paucibacillary by lepromin but multibacillary by smear.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman develops tense blisters on normal and erythematous skin. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone. The blister forms subepidermally. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ on DIF. Blisters are tense (subepidermal), occur on normal and erythematous skin, and affect older adults. The target antigen is BP180 (type XVII collagen) and BP230.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive male develops painful grouped vesicles along the T5 dermatome. He has had three such episodes in the past year. What prophylactic measure is recommended?
opts: Oral valacyclovir 1g once daily for 5 days each episode
questions.exp: Recurrent herpes zoster in immunocompromised patients warrants chronic suppressive therapy. Oral acyclovir 400mg twice daily (or valacyclovir 500mg once daily) is used as long-term suppression for recurrent zoster/herpes in HIV patients.

questions.q: A 25-year-old sexually active male has a painless indurated ulcer on the glans with a clean base and hard non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Dark-field microscopy shows motile spirochetes. Treatment of choice is?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (painless indurated chancre + hard non-tender lymphadenopathy) caused by Treponema pallidum. First-line treatment is benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM as a single dose. Dark-field microscopy is diagnostic in primary/secondary syphilis.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman has a 2cm pearly nodule on her nose with telangiectasia and central ulceration. She has had extensive sun exposure. The most common type of this tumour is?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common skin cancer. The nodular type is the most common subtype (~60-70%), presenting as a pearly nodule with rolled borders, telangiectasia, and central ulceration on sun-exposed areas.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman has butterfly-shaped erythema on her face, oral ulcers, and polyarthritis. ANA is positive (1:640). Anti-dsDNA is elevated. Complement C3 and C4 are low. Renal biopsy shows mesangial hypercellularity. What WHO/ISN class of lupus nephritis is this?
questions.exp: Class II lupus nephritis (mesangial proliferative) is characterized by mesangial hypercellularity and matrix expansion on biopsy. It generally has a good prognosis compared to class III/IV. Presentation with mild proteinuria/hematuria fits.

questions.q: A 20-year-old develops itchy vesicles on the elbows, knees, and buttocks. DIF shows granular IgA deposits at the dermal papillae tips. He also has chronic diarrhoea. What is the first-line treatment?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is associated with coeliac disease. DIF shows granular IgA at dermal papillae tips (pathognomonic). Dapsone provides rapid symptomatic relief; a gluten-free diet is the definitive treatment and may allow dapsone to be tapered.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male on long-term chlorpromazine therapy develops a blue-grey discolouration predominantly on sun-exposed facial skin. This pigmentary change is best attributed to?
questions.exp: Long-term phenothiazines (chlorpromazine) cause slate-grey/blue-grey pigmentation on sun-exposed skin. Histology shows drug-melanin complexes and melanin in dermal macrophages. The mechanism involves drug metabolites binding to melanin.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman develops sclerodactyly, digital pitting scars, and bilateral pulmonary fibrosis. ANA shows anti-centromere pattern. She has had Raynaud's phenomenon for 10 years. Which diagnosis does this best fit?
questions.exp: Anti-centromere antibodies are characteristic of limited cutaneous SSc (CREST syndrome: Calcinosis, Raynaud's, oEsophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia). Long-standing Raynaud's preceding other features is typical of limited SSc.

questions.q: A 16-year-old presents with tinea capitis showing kerion formation – a boggy, tender, suppurative mass with broken hair stubs. Culture grows Microsporum canis. The treatment of choice is?
opts: Oral griseofulvin with topical antifungal shampoo
questions.exp: Tinea capitis requires systemic antifungal (topical fails to penetrate hair follicles). Griseofulvin remains first-line for Microsporum species. Terbinafine is preferred for Trichophyton species. Adjunctive antifungal shampoo reduces shedding and spread.

questions.q: A 68-year-old male has a rapidly growing ulcerated nodule on his lower lip that has enlarged from 1cm to 3cm in 6 weeks. He smokes and has chronic sun damage. Histology shows squamous cell nests with central keratin pearls invading the dermis. The worst prognostic factor is?
questions.exp: Perineural invasion is an independent poor prognostic factor in squamous cell carcinoma, associated with higher rates of local recurrence, regional metastasis, and disease-specific mortality. Tumour size >2cm and poorly differentiated histology also worsen prognosis, but perineural invasion carries the highest risk.

questions.q: A nurse develops painful erythematous nodules on the anterior shins. She was recently diagnosed with sarcoidosis. Blood cultures are negative. The most appropriate next step is?
opts: NSAIDs and bed rest with leg elevation
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum is the clinical diagnosis (tender nodules on anterior shins). It is a reactive panniculitis, not an infection. Treatment is symptomatic with NSAIDs, bed rest, and leg elevation. Biopsy is not needed for classic presentation; corticosteroids are reserved for severe or persistent cases.

questions.q: A 24-year-old woman presents with sharply demarcated depigmented patches on her hands and perioral area. Woods lamp shows bright white fluorescence. She has vitiligo. Which investigation is NOT routinely recommended in workup?
questions.exp: Vitiligo is associated with autoimmune conditions including thyroid disease, diabetes mellitus, and pernicious anaemia. TSH, fasting glucose, and CBC (for pernicious anaemia) are appropriate screening. MRI brain has no role in routine vitiligo workup.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male smoker has a painless genital ulcer that is NOT indurated, with ragged undermined edges. The base is dirty. The inguinal lymph nodes are tender and fluctuant (bubo). Gram stain shows 'school of fish' appearance. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Chancroid presents with painful, soft, non-indurated ulcer with ragged undermined edges and dirty base. Painful inguinal adenopathy forming buboes is characteristic. Gram stain shows the classic 'school of fish' pattern of H. ducreyi.

questions.q: An 8-year-old child has circular scaly patches on the scalp with fluorescence under Wood's lamp. KOH mount shows ectothrix pattern. Which dermatophyte is most likely?
questions.exp: Microsporum audouinii and M. canis cause ectothrix tinea capitis with bright green fluorescence under Wood's lamp. Trichophyton species are endothrix (no Wood's lamp fluorescence). Epidermophyton does not infect hair.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male develops blisters in the mouth and then on the skin. The blisters are flaccid and easily rupture. DIF shows intercellular IgG ('fish net' pattern) in the epidermis. The target antigen is?
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris targets desmoglein 3 (oral mucosa involvement) and desmoglein 1 (skin involvement). DIF shows intercellular IgG giving the pathognomonic 'fish net/chicken wire' pattern. Flaccid blisters with positive Nikolsky sign are characteristic.

questions.q: A 35-year-old male on dapsone for leprosy develops pallor, jaundice, and fatigue. His haemoglobin drops to 7.5g/dL. His G6PD level is markedly low. What is the mechanism of this haemolytic anaemia?
opts: Direct oxidative damage to RBCs overwhelming glutathione defence
Aplastic crisis due to bone marrow suppression
questions.exp: Dapsone causes dose-dependent oxidative haemolysis. G6PD-deficient patients are at higher risk as they cannot regenerate reduced glutathione. Dapsone's hydroxylamine metabolite oxidises haemoglobin to methaemoglobin and causes Heinz body haemolysis.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with a solitary flesh-coloured plaque on the glans penis for 2 years. Biopsy shows full-thickness epidermal dysplasia without invasion. This is best termed?
questions.exp: Erythroplasia of Queyrat is SCC in situ affecting the glans penis. It presents as a velvety red plaque (though this case shows flesh colour – early lesions can vary). It is the penile equivalent of Bowen disease and has a higher rate of progression to invasive SCC.

questions.q: A patient with longstanding psoriasis undergoes a Tzanck smear from a blistered lesion. This would be diagnostically helpful in which of the following conditions?
questions.exp: Tzanck smear detects acantholytic cells (rounded keratinocytes with large nuclei) in pemphigus and multinucleated giant cells in herpetic infections. It is not useful for psoriasis, bullous pemphigoid, or EB. Pemphigus vulgaris is the correct answer.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with symmetric non-scarring alopecia in a band-like distribution along the frontal hairline. The scalp shows mild erythema and scaling. Pull test is negative. This pattern is most consistent with?
questions.exp: Frontal fibrosing alopecia (FFA) presents with a band-like recession of the frontal and temporal hairline with perifollicular erythema and scaling. It is a form of lichen planopilaris causing cicatricial alopecia, more common in postmenopausal women but increasingly seen in younger women.

questions.q: An infant presents at birth with large blisters that form after minimal trauma. The blisters heal without scarring. Electron microscopy shows cleavage within the lamina lucida. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Junctional EB has cleavage within the lamina lucida (between the plasma membrane of basal cells and the lamina densa). Mutations affect laminin-332 or type XVII collagen. Blisters heal without scarring (unlike dystrophic EB which scars/milia). Herlitz type is fatal in infancy.

questions.q: A 48-year-old male presents with hyperpigmented, verrucous plaques in the axillae, neck folds, and groin. He has a BMI of 38. Biopsy shows papillomatosis and hyperkeratosis with minimal acanthosis. This finding should prompt investigation for?
questions.exp: Acanthosis nigricans in an obese patient most commonly reflects insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes (benign AN). Fasting glucose and insulin levels should be checked. Malignant AN (associated with gastric adenocarcinoma) is rapid-onset, extensive, and occurs in non-obese adults.

questions.q: A 27-year-old woman has painful punched-out leg ulcers, livedo reticularis, and a history of recurrent DVT. Coagulation studies show prolonged APTT not corrected by mixing study. The underlying dermatological condition is caused by?
questions.exp: Antiphospholipid syndrome presents with thrombosis (DVT), livedo reticularis, skin ulcers, and obstetric complications. Prolonged APTT not corrected on mixing (lupus anticoagulant effect) confirms the diagnosis. Livedoid vasculopathy-like ulcers occur due to thrombotic occlusion.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on multidrug therapy develops sudden worsening of existing lesions with new erythematous tender skin nodules, fever, and iritis. ENL reaction is suspected. The first-line treatment is?
questions.exp: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) is a type 2 lepra reaction. MDT must NEVER be stopped. First-line is prednisolone (systemic corticosteroids). Thalidomide is very effective and can be used in males or non-pregnant women for recurrent ENL, but corticosteroids are the standard first-line. Clofazimine is used for chronic/recurrent ENL.

questions.q: A 19-year-old presents with hypopigmented macules over the trunk with fine 'cigarette paper' scaling. KOH mount shows 'spaghetti and meatballs' appearance. The causative organism requires which supplement to grow in culture?
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor is caused by Malassezia furfur (Pityrosporum orbiculare), a lipophilic yeast. It requires lipid-enriched (olive oil overlay) media like Dixon agar for in vitro culture, as it cannot synthesise C12-C14 fatty acids. KOH shows the classic 'spaghetti and meatballs' appearance.

questions.q: A 55-year-old with rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate develops painful oral erosions, skin erosions, and eye involvement. Nikolsky sign is positive. This serious drug reaction mimics which condition immunologically?
questions.exp: Toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) is a severe drug reaction with epidermal detachment >30% BSA, mucositis, and positive Nikolsky sign. It carries high mortality (SCORTEN score). Methotrexate is a known causative drug. SJS (<10% BSA) and SJS/TEN overlap (10-30%) are related.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child develops honey-coloured crusted lesions around the nose and mouth. Gram stain shows gram-positive cocci in clusters. Which complication is specific to this condition and NOT caused by pharyngeal infection with the same organism?
questions.exp: Impetigo caused by nephritogenic strains of Streptococcus pyogenes can cause post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN). Crucially, PSGN follows both cutaneous and pharyngeal GAS infection, BUT rheumatic fever follows ONLY pharyngeal infection, not skin infection. This is the key distinguishing fact.

questions.q: During a patch test procedure, the readings are taken at 48 hours and again at 96 hours. A reaction that appears at 48h but fades by 96h is most likely?
questions.exp: In patch testing, irritant reactions tend to peak early (at 48h) and fade by 96h, following a 'decrescendo' pattern. True allergic contact dermatitis reactions persist or intensify between 48h and 96h readings ('crescendo' pattern). This distinction helps differentiate true sensitisation from false-positive irritant responses.
